clue.text: Player's challenge? I sympathise

definitions.meaning: an actor facing a tough speech has difficult ... to learn
a commiserating phrase meaning bad luck, said to someone unfortunate

explanation.surface: A competitor faces a tough test and a friend offers sympathy.
explanation.walkthrough: The second light, 16, completes the phrase. 'Player' is an actor here, not a sportsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally tough script for an actor; idiomatically a British expression of commiseration for bad luck.

clue.text: Awful swindle turned up evidence of debts

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the word for swindle is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to do someone is to swindle them
IOUs are written acknowledgements of money owed

explanation.surface: A terrible con brings to light records of what someone owes.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something hateful or extremely unpleasant; synonyms.

clue.text: Transform from 27 to 1 as unusually polemic act

indicators.note: unusually says the letters of polemic act are set in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A controversial deed changes things in an unusual way.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 is EASY and 1 is HARD, so the definition means turn easy into hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Making something easy into something hard is to make it more involved and difficult.

clue.text: No difficulty in this riddle, initially? Au contraire!

definitions.text: No difficulty in this riddle, initially? Au contraire!

indicators.note: in says the word for no difficulty sits inside the two initial letters
initially takes the opening letters of this and riddle

parts.note: ease is freedom from difficulty

explanation.surface: The setter claims the riddle is easy, then cheekily contradicts himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Au contraire!' turns the whole clue into the definition: a puzzle that is the opposite of no difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: A brain-teaser is a puzzle that gives real difficulty, the reverse of being easy.

clue.text: Be amorous, giving ring with love in romantic light?

indicators.note: in places the ring and the love inside the romantic light

parts.note: a candle gives the soft light of a romantic dinner
a ring is round, the shape of the letter O
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A proposal by candlelight: offering a ring with love.
explanation.definitionFit: To kiss and cuddle is to behave amorously; a jocular synonym.

clue.text: Club, maybe, that footballer tries to avoid

definitions.meaning: clubs is a suit, so a club is one kind of playing piece in a pack
a referee shows a yellow or red one for a foul

explanation.surface: A football club is something a player would rather steer clear of.
explanation.definitionFit: A club is one suit of playing pieces, and referees book players by showing coloured ones.

clue.text: Something tough, mostly appropriate, repeated about work

indicators.note: about says the repeated word goes round the word for work
repeated says the shortened word is written twice
mostly drops the last letter of the word for appropriate

parts.note: to nick something is to appropriate or steal it
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A hard task, suitable for doing over and over at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' and 'repeated' make NICNIC, which 'about' wraps round the work; 'appropriate' is the verb meaning steal, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a difficult or unpleasant experience, the opposite of an easy outing.

clue.text: Vehicle trapped by one tramcar after another

indicators.note: trapped by says the answer lies caught within the words that follow
one tramcar after another asks for the word tramcar written twice in a row

parts.note: a single tramcar, the word as written

explanation.surface: A vehicle is stuck in traffic between a line of trams.
explanation.walkthrough: Writing TRAMCARTRAMCAR, the answer spans the join; 'one' is part of the phrase 'one ... after another'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cart is a simple wheeled vehicle, often horse-drawn.

clue.text: Princess attached to rock stars in group

definitions.meaning: in Greek myth the Ethiopian princess was chained to a rock to be devoured by a sea monster
a northern constellation, a group of stars, named after her

explanation.surface: A royal clings to her rock-star group.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical princess rescued by Perseus also gives her name to a constellation and galaxy.

clue.text: Subtle charm of a city for the natives

parts.note: Italians call their capital Roma

explanation.surface: A city has a subtle allure for those who live there.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, an aura or pervading quality, a subtle air about something.

clue.text: Don't hold up surgeon, say, over one's work

parts.note: a surgeon is an example of a doctor, abbreviated Dr
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
op, short for opus, is a composer's numbered work

explanation.surface: Someone urges a surgeon not to delay an operation.
explanation.definitionFit: To sag or hang down is the opposite of holding oneself up.

clue.text: Winter driving problem, a mixture of wind and frost

indicators.note: a mixture of says the letters of wind and frost are mixed together

explanation.surface: Wind and frost together make winter roads treacherous.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank of wind-blown snow blocking a road is a hazard for motorists in winter.

clue.text: Person who handles notes son kept in notebook

indicators.note: kept in says the abbreviation for son is held inside the notebook word

parts.note: cahier is French for an exercise book or notebook, used in English too

explanation.surface: A child keeps a jotter, as a note-handler might.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank or shop teller handles banknotes and cash.

clue.text: See 27
Trade outside preserve of church dignitary

indicators.note: outside says the word for trade goes round the word for preserve

parts.note: to deal is to trade
to can food is to preserve it

explanation.surface: Commerce surrounds a cleric's jam-making.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to a dean, a senior cathedral cleric.

clue.text: Awfully silly chap hiding bad mark in trivial task

indicators.note: hiding says the shuffled letters close around the bad mark
awfully says the letters of silly chap are badly jumbled

parts.note: D is a poor grade in an exam

explanation.surface: A foolish fellow conceals a poor grade in an easy assignment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' rearranges SILLYCHAP, and 'hiding' puts D inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for something so easy a young one could manage it.

clue.text: See 1
Confused, as the Queen's Navee leader never was

definitions.text: as the Queen's Navee leader never was
definitions.meaning: in Gilbert and Sullivan's HMS Pinafore, Sir Joseph Porter stuck close to his desk and never went to sea, yet became ruler of the Queen's Navee

explanation.surface: A comic-opera admiral, bewildered, never set sail.
explanation.definitionFit: Lost and bewildered, like a ship far from land; and literally out on the ocean.

clue.text: Transform from 1 to 27 — second hint provided inside

indicators.note: inside says the word for provided goes within the word for hint

parts.note: to imply is to hint
if means provided, on condition that

explanation.surface: A second clue is given within to help transform things.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 is HARD and 27 is EASY: turning hard into easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Making something hard easy is to make it less complicated.

clue.text: Alternative to piece of cake as epitome of ease

definitions.text: Alternative to piece of cake as epitome of ease

parts.words: Alternative to piece of cake as epitome of ease
parts.note: 'easy as ...' uses a different baked dish from 'a piece of cake' to mean simple

explanation.surface: Another dessert stands for something effortless.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'easy as' this dish is a stock simile for something very simple.

clue.text: Request lowly worker to hold it up twice

indicators.note: to hold says the lowly worker surrounds the rest

parts.note: a peon is a labourer of low status

indicators.note: twice says the word it is written two times
in a down clue, up means the word it is read bottom to top

explanation.surface: A humble labourer is asked to lift something twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns IT into TI and 'twice' doubles that to TITI.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal written appeal or plea is a request.

clue.text: Like some old Americans captured on film?

definitions.meaning: relating to the Inca people of pre-Columbian Peru
a scene filmed and complete is in the can, read as two words

explanation.surface: Ancient Americans have been recorded on camera.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective for the Inca civilisation; split, it is the film phrase for a finished take.

clue.text: Dreadful summer with minimal temperature — most odd

indicators.note: dreadful says the letters of summer are badly mangled
minimal takes only the smallest part, the first letter, of temperature

clue.text: Works out what's 500 in twos

parts.note: deuces are twos in cards or dice

clue.text: Grave indications for dogs

definitions.meaning: piles of stones mark burial sites or summits
a breed of small Scottish terrier

explanation.surface: Solemn signs pointing to dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Stone mounds often mark graves, and the Scottish terrier breed shares the name.

clue.text: Composed arrangement for cello etc, then died

indicators.note: an arrangement for instruments rearranges the letters of cello etc

explanation.surface: A composer writes an arrangement for strings then passes away.
explanation.definitionFit: Calm and self-possessed; a synonym in the sense of collected oneself.

clue.text: Discarded queen, perhaps, retaining spades

parts.note: a queen is a female cat

explanation.surface: A card player throws away a queen but keeps a spade.
explanation.walkthrough: The queen is not a card but a female cat.

clue.text: Point ace secured in superlative finish

parts.note: -est is the ending of a superlative adjective
A is the abbreviation for ace on playing cards

explanation.definitionFit: One of the four cardinal points of the compass.

clue.text: Prepare to fire two or three, for instance

definitions.meaning: to load a gun with powder, ready to shoot
numbers divisible only by one and themselves

explanation.surface: Getting ready to shoot two or three rounds.

clue.text: Academic sinecure? It supports one comfortably

clue.text: Some features of a sitting room

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next
